lesson.subtitle: Lesson 27 -- The First Concession
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Flávio Masaharu Kuroda | Lesson 27 -- The First Concession
lesson.grammar_point: first conditional for trade-offs (if you sign..., we will...; if we..., will you...?)

listenings.text: The first discount you give is the most important one, because it teaches the buyer how you negotiate. If you give it for free, the buyer will ask for more. So my first rule is simple: never give, always trade. Put the condition first and the gift second. If you sign for three years, we will reduce the price. If you pay annually, we will throw in the training. My second rule: make the first concession small. If you start with twenty percent, the buyer will think your list price was never real. My third rule: when the buyer asks you to meet halfway, do not say yes at once. Ask a question first. If we do that, will you sign this week?

I buy software for a living, and I ask for a discount in the first meeting, every time, even when the price is fair. I want to see how much wiggle room the seller has. Last month, one seller gave me fifteen percent in the first minute. I thanked him, and then I asked for more, because now I knew his list price was not serious. Another seller said: if you commit to a multi-year deal, we can do eight percent. I asked for ten. She said: if you sign by Friday, we will do ten. That was the deal I signed. She gave me something, but every time she asked for something in return.
